subject.title: fix: stop doctor misreporting trusted-proxy gateways as unauthenticated

question: Should Doctor treat a runtime-valid, host-scoped trusted-proxy configuration as authentication proof for the exposed-Gateway finding while retaining the proposed proxy-source and Control UI origin critical checks?
rationale: This is a policy decision about what a security diagnostic should certify, not a mechanical defect that review automation can settle from tests alone.

options.title: Approve the bounded diagnostic policy
options.body: Accept the runtime-aligned readiness predicate after the branch is refreshed and its exact-head security proof is rerun.

options.title: Keep the current unauthenticated critical
options.body: Require a shared token or password for this Doctor classification and leave trusted-proxy deployments on the existing critical path.

options.title: Request a narrower diagnostic distinction
options.body: Keep trusted-proxy awareness but use separate language that avoids treating the configuration as equivalent to shared-secret authentication.

recommendation.title: Approve the bounded diagnostic policy
recommendation.body: Accept the runtime-aligned readiness predicate after the branch is refreshed and its exact-head security proof is rerun.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the concrete contract analysis and can respond to a security-owner decision, though final policy approval should come from the gateway-security area owner.
